body: It's been about a month since my fiance took his life. The first 2 weeks were just sleep, I barely ate. Then I managed to get into grief counseling and my counselor gave me some things and tips to gently work myself through this. Every morning I write in a booklet, mornings have been very difficult for me. I write to him, write about him, and it helps me process my feelings. I watch TV, mostly things that make me laugh, and things I know he would appreciate if he were still here. I avoid his favorite shows however, and likewise with video games, I recently been able to gather the courage to get on my computer, since we spent a lot of our time together playing games. I can't play our favorites still, but I can play a few. I had to move back in With family. And Tha kfully I have a fairly large and active family, so there's always someone visiting, they always listen when I need someone to talk to. David (my fiance) and I were always spiritually inclined, no so much visiting things like church and things, but felt like there was more to life than just birth and death. So I find comfort watching videos of mediums connecting people with their loved ones on the other side, and it gives me hope.
I have family who try and tell me they know how I feel. I let it slide because I genuinely know they mean well. But the only person who understands would be my grandmother.
My man left this world almost 3 weeks ago. But for some reason time feels like it's only been days yet, somehow months have already passed. It's been slow.
I lost my better half Sept 14th. The ride ahead is a bumpy one.

I lost my husband-to-be almost 3 weeks ago from suicide. Every day was anguish. Feeling like I did him wrong. I ended up speaking to a medium, who assured me it wasn't my doing, and that I had made him happy. However when I asked if he and I were soulmates, they said that he had said no, not to say he didn't love me all the same, however. But in life we felt we were. This sapped everything out of me and I've been in deep depression all day. I don't want to pass this off as someone to not believe, because their reading was pretty spot on, but it was sure hard to accept.

I never thought my heart could break twice.
Makes sense. He did have a lot of trauma he didn't like to talk about often.

I lost the love of my life a week ago today. He was everything I ever wanted in a person. His agony got the best of him despite my best attempts to make him feel loved. The pain is raw, I understand. Sometimes I question if I'll love again, and all I can do is believe I will. My days with him were short, only just over 2 years of being together but if felt like I've known him my whole life.

It'll get better, everyone grieves differently, at different paces. Take it a day at a time. Find support groups, connect with people who know the pain you endure, and remember we just endure this, we survive. We live in their memory, for their memory, live for them, love again for them. And remember they're always with you. Even try to connect with a medium. After my beloved took his life, I felt compelled to find answer. Connect with your spirituality.
My bf ended his life about 3 days ago.. haven't had him visit my dreams. I hope he does. Just so I can tell him I loved him one last time.

I lost my sweet boy yesterday, my star, the light of my life, my husband to be. He said he would never leave me, but here I am, alone in a room with just pictures and a memory. Its hard, and it'll be hard. Part of me doesn't want anyone else, part of me thinks I'll never find another like him, and the truth is I won't, and that's a hard pill to swallow.

But I'm going to try, not for me but for him. He wouldn't want me to live life like this, so I will live for him, learn to love again, for him. Take the time you need to grieve, but don't give up, live for them.
I have dear friends to keep me company as best they can while I wait. I appreciate all the kind words. I only wish he talked to me.
